feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear progression, relevant scope, and solid technical breadth. It reads professionally and is mostly polished, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, more quantified outcomes, and a few wording/style fixes to improve consistency and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong relevance for digital strategy roles: web, CMS, analytics, governance, email, social, and multimedia are all well covered.  
- Good credibility through concrete scale indicators such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope/activity: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; the CV repeats similar themes and could be streamlined for sharper structure.  
- Fix minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with a sharper value proposition, one or two concrete signals of scale, and slightly less overlap with the skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” and tighten phrasing for a more polished executive tone.
- Add one concrete scope marker from recent roles, such as leading a 10,000+ page Drupal migration or supporting 3.5M annual page views.
- Emphasize current positioning: digital strategy, platform modernization, governance, analytics, and mission-driven communications leadership.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, digital governance, and workflow design, with a track record of leading large-scale web and content operations. Strong in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” repeat heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” also appear elsewhere; keep them here only if central to target roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level strengths will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, sharper phrasing and favor higher-value capabilities over generic terms like “multi-channel communication.”
- Replace with: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Editorial operations & governance • Web platform & CMS leadership • Cross-channel content strategy • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Consider “Cross-channel content strategy” instead of “Multi-channel communication” for stronger leadership positioning.
- Consider “Editorial operations & governance” to better reflect the CV’s repeated emphasis on standards, planning, and publishing systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it concise and avoid listing specific tools already covered elsewhere.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design”; combining them avoids redundancy.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and only the most current/high-value contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance models to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Consolidate build work into one bullet: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable toolkits for member engagement.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, users reached, publishing time reduced, search success improved, or campaign engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and the microsite/toolkit work duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold specifics.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement also echo the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize advisory/consulting capacity and new initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullets into one flagship achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused: replace “reaching tens of thousands / serving thousands” with stronger metrics if available (growth, engagement, open rates, campaign performance, production volume).
- Tighten operations/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio” and “Expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program expansion also appears in earlier roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house capability here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo role above it. Tighten it around executional leadership, cross-team coordination, and channel growth, with any concrete volume or cadence metrics you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-led: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague workflow bullets with specifics if possible: “Built cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved coordination among communications, advocacy and program teams.” Add any measurable result (faster turnaround, higher output, fewer errors).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved workflows” and “strengthened coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullets; keep this item focused on hands-on execution rather than enterprise leadership.
- Weekly video work also appears in the earlier 2015–2018 role and footer project list; emphasize scaling/ownership here, not origin.

- “Audience-focused content planning” is close to existing storytelling/editorial planning language in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability areas; keep only the most market-significant platforms.
- Cut lower-priority items already covered elsewhere (e.g., jQuery, Airtable systems).

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:

items.title: University of Virginia

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platforms, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” It should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise site architecture, migrations, modular content builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, order by strength/relevance: **Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** to reflect recent public-sector platform leadership.
- Consider replacing weaker/older tools with a qualifier if accurate, e.g. **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views)** to add impact.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid listing platforms here if they are already better covered under Topline Skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the seniority of the profile unless tied to a specific use case or removed.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the role specifically requires them; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more current.
- Consider grouping by function for readability: Front-end: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, jQuery | Integration/Tagging: APIs, Google Tag Manager | DevOps/Edge: GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers
- If possible, add evidence in recent roles instead of here, e.g., “built custom Drupal front-end components,” “implemented GTM tagging,” or “used GitHub Actions for deployment workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- If Cloudflare Workers/GitHub Actions are minor exposure only, consider removing them to avoid overstating depth.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since automation is already emphasized in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly grouped to signal systems depth without repeating the same message.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not as one long list: “Automation & Workflow Systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Work Management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier should lead because they align with your recent workflow/operations work.
- Standardize naming for polish: use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams.”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one tool to impact in experience bullets (e.g., Airtable/Power Automate used to streamline editorial planning or cross-team publishing workflows).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap as project-management tools; consider trimming one or two if space is tight.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too generic and underplays your stronger, recent email leadership in NACo roles. Make it more specific and ordered by enterprise relevance, not just a raw list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder for credibility and recency: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of only product names: **Higher Logic (member email/newsletters) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration/CRM-linked campaigns) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**
- Keep vendor names concise; consider shortening **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys** to **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights (Journeys)** for readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and multi-channel communications; avoid repeating outcomes here unless you remove them from role bullets.
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate Higher Logic’s community/member functions unless clarified as email/member engagement.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” team-building, and concrete outputs from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add sharper execution language: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates for member and advocacy communications.”
- Clarify management contribution without overstating: “Provided day-to-day direction and production support for a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this item focused on launching/establishing the format, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple roles; specify what changed or what channels/processes were improved.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation, research support, and first-of-its-kind multimedia work.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities, while expanding NACo’s early digital content capabilities.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten the phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague wording like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a clearer outcome-oriented phrase such as “produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience/downloads, or types of research/projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/multimedia leadership here; later entries show that progression more credibly.
